title: containerd vs Kubernetes: practical decision guide
description: Compare containerd and Kubernetes by intended use, workflow fit, integrations, administration, security, and total cost. PilotStack does not declare a universal winner without verified, current evidence; check official vendor documentation and plan terms before deciding.

verdict: There is no verified universal winner between containerd and Kubernetes in this guide. Start with the job to be done, test both products against the same representative workflow, and record the results against written criteria. Confirm current features, plan limits, integrations, privacy, access controls, support, migration, and total cost using official vendor sources before committing. If the products serve different primary purposes, treat them as potentially complementary rather than interchangeable.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between containerd and Kubernetes?
faqs.answer: Compare the actual workflows and outcomes each product supports for your team. Verify current capabilities with the vendors rather than relying on unsourced ratings or old feature claims.

faqs.question: Which is better, containerd or Kubernetes?
faqs.answer: The better fit depends on your requirements. Pilot both against the same written criteria and select the product that meets the critical needs with acceptable cost and operational risk.

faqs.question: How should I compare pricing?
faqs.answer: Use current official pricing and include seats, usage, required tiers, integrations, implementation, support, and ongoing administration. Do not rely on old prices shown in third-party summaries.

faqs.question: What should I verify before switching?
faqs.answer: Check data export and migration, access controls, integrations, retention, support, contract terms, and any workflow that must not be interrupted.
